children: IAG expects 2026 capacity to fall slightly year over year, the first decline since 2022, citing lost Middle East flying, regional conflict disruptions and higher fuel costs as it prioritises profit.
IAG shares rose to 437 pence Friday, their highest since Aug. 24, after results. They were up 13.7% from the month's low and had traded between 395 and 448 pence since July 16.
IAG’s January–September British Airways profit fell 8.8% to £1.493 billion, while Aer Lingus profit more than halved to €108 million. IAG Loyalty profit rose 17.7% to £391 million.
IAG now expects 12 aircraft deliveries in 2026, down from 16. The cut includes three Boeing 737s. Vueling’s first Boeing delivery date remains unclear due to delayed seat certification.
IAG CEO Luis Gallego said TAP’s proposed sale terms did not fit the group’s plans. IAG will grow Brazil routes through Iberia and explore other regional partnerships.
